text:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated packet jitter observed in az1a affecting inference GRPC streams. p95 token latency up, grpc retry rate ~8%. linking runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/net-az-jitter

mike: ack, I'm on it. grabbing metrics and recent host logs.

sara: seeing bursts from g5-ephemeral pool, RX jitter + tx reorder around 16:24 UTC. resolver latencies spiking (~350-500ms) at same intervals.

jason: can we move shared traffic off az1a to nearby AZs temporarily? steering policy allows cross-az respill. prepping traffic-reshuffle command.

ops-bot: runbook step: increase ephemeral capacity +20% (cmd: /infra scale ephemeral-pool --percent 20)

mike: scaled ephemeral pool +25% (started). new instances booting, KV cache will be cold for a few mins.

sara: note — customers with Reserved/Dedicated capacity not impacted. shared API customers seeing tail errors and transient 5xx. posting internal customer impact sheet: https://go/redwood/incidents/7165823450/impact

jason: issued traffic reshuffle via steering service: `curl -s -X POST https://steer.redwood/api/reshuffle -d '{"from":"az1a","to":"az1b,eu-west1a","weight":0.45}'` — monitoring. Expect short blip while routing converges.

mike: after reshuffle p95 down from ~420ms -> ~160ms, 5xx rate down 8% -> 2%. KV miss spike observed for ~90s.

sara: dropping resolver timeout threshold on proxy to avoid long tails (config push in progress).

jason: started a lightweight canary to verify model loads on target AZs — all good.

mike: customers: no major upticks in support tickets yet but some throttles in telemetry. flagging accounts with strict SLOs for follow-up.

kristin: I'm taking oncall handover in 30m. leave notes about the reshuffle and cache warmup. I'll keep the bridge open for another hour.

ops-bot: BRIDGE_CREATED: https://zoom.redwood/7165823450 (opened by jason)

mike: leaving detailed notes in the incident doc and handing to kristin. key actions: scaled ephemeral +25%, traffic reshuffle executed, resolver timeout lowered, monitoring shows steady recovery.

sara: recommend follow-up: run packet captures on affected hosts, validate host NIC firmware versions, and consider scheduled capacity shift if trend repeats.

kristin: ack. I'll kick off packet captures and coordinate with infra tomorrow AM if we see reoccur. closing active mitigation but keeping watch. :thumbsup:
